parts.name: duodenoscopeElevator
parts.what: Distal tip of a duodenoscope close-up, side-viewing, showing the elevator mechanism and its narrow recess, ideally open and closed.. Teaches: Why the elevator recess is a documented outbreak site: it directs accessories, is narrow and mechanically complex, and is extremely difficult to clean.

parts.name: leakTestSetup
parts.what: Flexible endoscope connected to a leak tester and immersed in water, with air bubbles escaping from a breach in the outer sheath.. Teaches: How a leak test shows a breach before immersion, since a breached scope admits fluid into an interior that cannot be cleaned.

parts.name: endoscopeReprocessor
parts.what: Automated endoscope reprocessor with lid open, a scope coiled in the basin and tubing connectors attached to its channels.. Teaches: How every channel must be attached to the correct model-specific connector, since an unconnected channel is not perfused or disinfected.

parts.name: dryingStorageCabinet
parts.what: Controlled drying and storage cabinet with flexible endoscopes hanging vertically and uncoiled, valves removed.. Teaches: Why scopes are stored hanging vertically and uncoiled with valves removed so channels drain and dry, unlike coiled storage that retains fluid.

parts.name: endoscopeChannels
parts.what: Cross-section or cutaway of the insertion tube showing several narrow channels of different diameters running its length.. Teaches: Why endoscopes are mechanically complex: multiple narrow channels of different diameters, some hard to access and easy to forget.

parts.name: channelBiofilm
parts.what: Longitudinal section of an endoscope channel with biofilm layer adhering to the channel wall, and a brush contacting the wall.. Teaches: Why only a brush touching the channel wall disrupts biofilm, and why soaking, flushing or chemical disinfection do not remove it.

parts.name: channelBrush
parts.what: Endoscope cleaning brush of the correct diameter and length passing through a channel, with the handle and bristle head shown.. Teaches: Why brush diameter and length matter and why brushing continues until the brush emerges visibly clean.
